answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a vertex as the anchor of the cost.
